open_copies.title_found: Robust deep learning based protein sequence design using ProteinMPNN
passages: Here we describe a deep learning based protein sequence design method, ProteinMPNN, with outstanding performance in both in silico and experimental tests.
We first tested the ability of ProteinMPNN to design amino acid sequences for protein backbones generated by deep network hallucination using AlphaFold (AF).
We set out to develop a deep learning based protein sequence design method broadly applicable to design of monomers, cyclic oligomers, protein nanoparticles, and protein-protein interfaces.

We started with a set of previously described protein backbones for two-component tetrahedral designs generated using a compute- and effort-intensive procedure that involved Rosetta sequence design followed by more than a week of manual intervention to eliminate unwanted substitutions (15).

The alpha-beta protein structure contains 5 beta strands and 4 alpha helices, and is close to the design target backbone (2.35 Å over 130 residues), demonstrating that ProteinMPNN can quite accurately encode monomer backbone geometry in amino acid sequences.
We next took advantage of the flexible decoding order of ProteinMPNN to design sequences for proteins containing internal repeats, tying the identities of proteins in equivalent positions.
